# Single standard deduction example recalculates live and shows the ordered estimate breakdown

> Prove the calculator recalculates live without submit or reload and presents the ordered estimate breakdown, gross income echo, Single standard deduction, and an allowed total label.

## Step 1

Open http://localhost:3000/bank-clone-app/calculators in desktop Chrome and confirm the Federal Income Tax Calculator is visible.

## Step 2

On the calculator page, enter annual income 85000, keep filing status set to Single, keep the standard deduction selected, and wait for the estimate panel to update while staying on the calculator page.

## Step 3

Assert the estimate panel lists Gross income, Deductions, Taxable income, Tax liability, and Taxes withheld in that order, and that the Gross income row shows $85,000 while the Deductions row shows $14,600.

## Step 4

Assert the Taxable income row shows $70,400, every visible calculator amount is formatted as whole-dollar US currency, and the total label is either "Estimated refund" or "Estimated amount you owe".

## Step 5

Confirm the estimate updated from typing alone, with no submit button interaction and no full page reload or hard navigation away from http://localhost:3000/bank-clone-app/calculators.

## Step 6 — assert @verifies ac-13, ac-14, ac-2, ac-3, ac-4, ac-5, ac-8, ac-9, ac-10, ac-12

Confirm absolute check: $70,400 (equals) — the stated promise: With an annual income of 85000, Single, and the standard deduction, the Taxable income row shows $70,400.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because it is the primary happy path on a money-related calculator and covers the broadest set of critical promises in one scenario/test pair.
[value_score] Scored next because the zero-floor boundary guards against negative taxable income across multiple representative inputs, a high-risk calculation defect.
[value_score] Scored just below sc-2 because the immediate-above-threshold case is the sharpest off-by-one boundary for the taxable-income formula.
[value_score] Scored above the remaining non-boundary paths because Married filing jointly changes the deduction amount materially and can misstate the estimate if wrong.
[value_score] Scored near sc-4 because Head of household is another distinct standard-deduction outcome that must not inherit the wrong filing-status amount.
[value_score] Scored lowest of the kept set because it proves a control reveal rather than a numeric outcome, though it still gates access to itemized deductions.

[self_critique] The oracle directly proved the PRD's explicit example taxable-income amount, the happy-path technique matched the representative example flow, no negative calculator case was omitted from this set because the PRD stated no invalid-input behavior for calculator fields, and the assertions stayed limited to values, labels, order, and live-update behavior the source named.

[self_critique] The oracle proved the floor-at-zero rule across the zero-outcome boundary representatives, boundary-value technique fit the threshold behavior, no separate negative case was required because this is a numeric boundary rather than an error-handling promise, and the assertions avoided overreach by checking only the threshold values and named display rules.

[self_critique] The oracle proved the same taxable-income formula on the first positive value above the threshold, boundary-value technique fit the off-by-one risk, no extra negative case was missing because the scenario's purpose was the positive-side boundary crossing, and the assertions stayed narrow to the named example state and allowed labels.

[self_critique] The oracle directly proved the Married filing jointly deduction amount, equivalence partitioning fit this outcome-changing filing-status path, no negative case was missing because the PRD did not define invalid filing-status behavior, and the assertions did not overstate any unstated tax-liability math.

[self_critique] The oracle directly proved the Head of household deduction amount, equivalence partitioning fit this distinct filing-status outcome, no negative case was missing because the source did not specify invalid-status handling, and the assertions remained limited to the deduction amount and shared display promises.

[self_critique] The oracle directly proved the Itemized-input reveal, equivalence partitioning fit the control-visibility change under deduction-type switching, no negative case was missing because the PRD did not state hidden/disabled behavior beyond the reveal itself, and the assertions avoided inventing any itemized-calculation rule the source never promised.
